nodes.title: The stack of persistent nodes
nodes.statement: For stable g,n, define N_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n}: its objects over S are stable ordered n-pointed families C/S together with a section q:S→Sing(C/S) of the scheme-theoretic relative singular locus. Arrows preserve q. Its pullback along a family C/S is canonically Sing(C/S), so N→M̄ is representable by schemes, finite and unramified, with empty pullback for a smooth family. Over N there is a finite étale degree-two scheme B→N of branches at the chosen node, and its ordering torsor is a torsor under the constant group C₂. This étaleness is over N, not over M̄ or an arbitrary smoothing base.
hypotheses: g,n≥0, 2g−2+n>0; base schemes are arbitrary; family, singular-scheme and gluing inputs are the parent contracts R1 and R2 below.
A chosen node is a section of Sing as a scheme, including its nilpotents. It need not exist on the whole base of a family with singular geometric fibres.
proofSteps: Pull back the parent relative singular scheme of the universal curve and use its formation under arbitrary base change to define the stack of pairs. The identification S×_{M̄}N=Sing(C/S) includes its structure sheaf.

The singular locus is closed in a proper curve, of finite presentation, and has finite geometric fibres. Proper and quasi-finite gives finite; nodality makes it unramified. On xy=a over R, it is Spec(R/(a)), since the relative Jacobian ideal is (x,y).

On the base of a chosen persistent node, use the parent local gluing/normalization contract: split xy=0 has two branches, and their permutations are étale transition data. Descend the two-element scheme and its ordering torsor. Every change of split nodal chart permutes the two branches and satisfies the cocycle.
acceptance: For xy=t over k[t], the node incidence is Spec k→Spec k[t], finite unramified and nonflat.
The branch-ordering cover has two geometric points in characteristic two; it is not μ₂.
A family pulled back into t=0 may have a persistent node even over a nonreduced base; use relative partial normalization rather than absolute normalization.

nodes.title: Clutching fibres as decorated node choices
nodes.statement: For a stable connected one-edge graph Γ with labelled external legs, let PΓ be the existing compactified vertex product and GΓ its constant finite label-preserving automorphism group. Let NΓ⊂N_{g,n} be the open-and-closed substack where partial normalization at the chosen node, with all other nodes retained, has the connected-component genera and external marking sets prescribed by Γ. Cutting and parent gluing give an equivalence [PΓ/GΓ]≃NΓ over M̄_{g,n}. The map PΓ→NΓ is a finite étale GΓ-torsor in the sense of stacks, even when GΓ acts with fixed isomorphism classes. For any C/S, S×_{M̄}PΓ is the scheme of Γ-decorated node choices on C/S; forgetting the decoration is finite étale over the corresponding open-and-closed subspace of Sing(C/S). Consequently both ordered clutching maps are representable finite unramified, without a global closed-immersion assertion.
hypotheses: The family-level inverse to gluing is supplied by R2: partial normalization at a persistent node, compatible with arbitrary base change and retaining every other node.
The original definitions of PΓ, GΓ and both clutching functors are imported without new copies. Γ has exactly one edge, and all its vertex types are stable.
proofSteps: Over the branch-ordering cover use relative partial normalization, locally R[x,y]/(xy)→R[x]×R[y], with equal constants giving the original ring. Replace only the selected node. For an external edge the result has two connected components; for a loop it is connected. In either case its new smooth sections carry the two flags. The parent genus and stability formulas give exactly the vertex types.

The gluing universal property and the relative partial-normalization comparison provide natural unit and counit isomorphisms on objects and arrows, compatible with base change. Thus this is an equivalence of groupoids over each scheme, not a count of geometric points.

For families with a chosen node, its separating/nonseparating character and the genus/leg partition of the cut components are étale locally constant: the relative cut is proper flat nodal and its connected components and their genera persist in the nodal deformation charts. Equivalently smoothing the unchosen edges contracts only edges other than the chosen one and preserves these data. Use the relative component/genus contract in R2, not absolute normalization of the total space.

Decorations are exactly identifications of these components/flags with Γ, a simply transitive GΓ-set after an étale cover. Descend their torsor. This proves the quotient equivalence and represents the fibre product by a finite étale cover of an open-and-closed part of Sing(C/S). Finiteness and unramifiedness then follow from persistent-node incidence; no argument infers étaleness over a smoothing base.
acceptance: The fibre-product equivalence fixes the target family and its gluing isomorphism; it therefore keeps two different chosen nodes even if an automorphism of the target exchanges them.
For a loop GΓ=C₂; for a separating edge it is C₂ exactly when g₁=g₂ and there are no external legs, and is trivial otherwise.
The three-elliptic-chain counterexample has two node choices of the same Γ and hence two distinct preimages in the same ordered separating source.
Use a relative cut over the actual base. Absolute normalization of a nonnormal or nonreduced total space is not this construction.

nodes.title: Node incidence on pointed boundary charts
nodes.statement: Let U→M̄_{g,n} be a sufficiently small étale scheme chart at a geometric stable curve with r nodes, with the independent smoothing coordinates t₁,…,tᵣ of the pointed normal-crossing chart. After further étale localization, U×_{M̄}N_{g,n}≅⨿_{j=1}^r V(tⱼ). The universal curve near the jth selected node has equation xⱼyⱼ=tⱼ after étale localization on curve and base. The chosen-node map V(tⱼ)→U is a regular codimension-one immersion and its conormal is (tⱼ)/(tⱼ²). On overlaps nodes can be permuted, and the corresponding local conormal lines identify coherently. For a map S→U, the node-incidence formula pulls back to ⨿V(tⱼ|S); that pullback need not be normal or Cartier.
hypotheses: U is an étale chart of the moduli stack itself over Z, not an arbitrary family base.

The pointed DM, universal-curve and normal-crossing results are imported from MC.2; the underlying unpointed versal parameters are MC.1. Parameters are local near a fixed finite set of nodes, after shrinking.
proofSteps: Start with the imported MC.1 versal node coordinates for g≥2. Extend to pointed types using the MC.2 universal-curve equivalence: adding a point at an old node replaces t by uv in the total base, while at a smooth point it adds a smooth coordinate; the new expanded curve has the corresponding two node parameters. Start separately at (0,3) and (1,1), as in the imported pointed DM proof. This is the chart form of that existing theorem, not a new moduli representability argument.

Use the parent arbitrary-base nodal normal form and the Jacobian calculation of incidence near each node. Finite unramified incidence can be étale locally separated into the chosen node branches, and after shrinking no additional singular points occur. Thus the jth branch is precisely V(tⱼ), with its scheme structure.

Since U is smooth over Z and the tⱼ are independent relative parameters, each V(tⱼ) is smooth over Z, hence regular and normal, and tⱼ is a nonzerodivisor. The unramified morphism has the displayed rank-one conormal. On a common chart refinement the chosen node determines the same local closed immersion; compare its ideal quotients and descend.
acceptance: For r=0 the incidence is empty and the boundary equation is the unit empty product.
At r=2 the total boundary is V(t₁t₂), while its two node branches are V(t₁) and V(t₂).
Over S mapping into tⱼ=0, pull back the conormal line from V(tⱼ); do not replace it by the ideal quotient of the zero ideal on S.

nodes.title: Chosen nodes and stack normalization
nodes.statement: Let Δ be the reduced total boundary of M̄_{g,n} over Z. Its normalization, in the sense of the imported DMNormalization construction, is canonically N_{g,n}. More explicitly, ⨿_{[Γ]}[PΓ/GΓ]≃N_{g,n}≃Δ^ν, compatibly with the maps to M̄_{g,n}. The normalization map is representable finite unramified and is an equivalence over the one-node boundary locus. The statement is about stacks: inertia that fixes a selected node remains, while automorphisms permuting distinct nodes act between different lifts. The construction agrees with R09.5 normalization on every smooth chart; no normalization/base-change claim for an arbitrary family base is included.
hypotheses: g,n≥0 in the stable range; Δ is the reduced relative normal-crossings boundary over Z.
Ordinary normalization means normalization of the reduction in its total rings of fractions. Z is an excellent Nagata base.
proofSteps: By node-atlas-branch-comparison, the incidence over U is ⨿V(tⱼ) and the reduced boundary has equation ∏tⱼ. These branches are normal; their disjoint union is the normalization of V(∏tⱼ), including when several j have the same global boundary type.

Invoke the already planned R09.5/dm-normalization and its smooth-chart characterization to glue this identification uniquely on atlas overlaps; invoke dm-normalization-finite for finiteness over Z. Do not construct stack normalization again here.

Use the relative decorated-node equivalence to identify the connected type pieces of N with the graph quotients. Over a one-node curve the node scheme is the base, so the incidence is an equivalence on that locus, including its stabilizers. Combine with the local branch computation to obtain the original boundary-normalization endpoint.
acceptance: On M̄₀,₃ the boundary, N and the coproduct of graph quotients are empty.
For (0,4), the normalization is the three boundary sections over Spec Z.
For (1,1), the boundary normalization is [M̄₀,₃/C₂]≃BC₂, not Spec Z. For (2,0), both Δ₀ and Δ₁ have the appropriate C₂ quotients.
At the two-tail genus-three curve N has two selected-node lifts in the same type piece; a global boundary component need not be embedded smoothly.

sources.match: Graph labels give finite étale covers of a fixed stratum, and the quotient of the compactified vertex product is its stack normalization. The relative one-edge comparison below includes further degenerations and labelled external markings.
Stack normalization is characterized by normalization on smooth scheme charts and glued from the normalized groupoid. R09.5 already owns this general construction.
Normal crossings give an unramified normalization locally equal to the separate regular divisor branches.

nodes.title: The integral smoothing conormal
nodes.statement: For j:N_{g,n}≃Δ^ν→M̄_{g,n}, construct the invertible conormal C_j by its étale-local description (t)/(t²) for the selected node branch, and its dual normal line C_j^∨. On the vertex-product cover PΓ→NΓ, give the canonical isomorphism C_j|PΓ≅L_a⊗L_b. The graph-equivariant structure uses ordinary unsigned symmetry when the flags are exchanged. In split charts a change of branch parameters x′=u₁x+O(x²), y′=v₁y+O(y²) on the cut central curve multiplies the smoothing conormal generator by u₁v₁; general lifts across the first infinitesimal neighborhood give the same law, regardless of their higher terms. These transitions satisfy composition, base-change and atlas-refinement coherence over Z, including characteristic two.
hypotheses: j is the finite unramified chosen-node map; its local closed-immersion charts are supplied by node-atlas-branch-comparison.

L_a,L_b are the imported marking cotangent lines on the cut curve, using their identification with branch differentials. The coordinates are formal parameters along the two smooth sections; their linear coefficients are units in the base ring.
This concerns the conormal of the chosen branch in the moduli stack. It is not the ideal of an arbitrary pulled-back boundary family, or the torsion differential on the singular curve.
proofSteps: On each pointed nodal moduli chart use the conormal of V(t) in U, and descend on common étale refinements. This produces a line because t is regular on the moduli chart. The native module for an affine ideal quotient is Ideal.Cotangent; scheme and stack sheafification remain supplier operations.

Compute the first-order smoothing class of xy=0 over any R by the relation module of the hypersurface: the map A²→A is (α,β)↦yα+xβ, and its cokernel is A/(x,y)=R, where A=R[x,y]/(xy). A perturbation of the equation contributes its value at the node; changes of lifted coordinates contribute a Jacobian term and disappear in this quotient. This computation, including nilpotents in R, shows that higher branch-parameter terms change no first-order multiplier. Comparing xy=t and x′y′=t′ gives [t′]=u₁v₁[t].

At each branch, [dx′]=u₁[dx] and [dy′]=v₁[dy]. Hence [t]↦[dx]⊗[dy] is independent of the split parameter choice. On overlaps with varying base coordinates use these pullback differential lines and the same relative Jacobian calculation. The product of slopes under composition is exactly the tensor transition cocycle. Polishchuk Proposition3.5 and Lemma4.6 provide an independent integral formal-coordinate check; Theorem1.2 over Q is not used.

For exchange x↔y, the relation xy and t are unchanged. The tensor identification exchanges the two factors by TensorProduct.comm without a sign. Descend the equivariant line along the constant GΓ-torsor and then along the moduli atlas by SF.1/stack-quasi-coherent. Invertibility and equality of maps can be checked after the faithfully flat cover. Use no averaging and no exactness claim for invariants.

Dualizing gives the normal line L_a^∨⊗L_b^∨; with a consumer’s integral or rational first-Chern-class API its class is −ψ_a−ψ_b. Only the class notation is imported from intersection theory, not a new Chow theory.
acceptance: Exchange must preserve the smoothing conormal over Z. The differential x dy instead changes to y dx=−x dy on xy=0 and is a different object.
The identification extends across extra nodes because it is made for the selected branch rather than only on the open one-node locus.
For a change x′=x+cx² on a branch, its slope is1, hence the induced conormal multiplier is1; nonlinear terms cannot create an extra factor.

sources.locator: Proposition3.5, §3.3, p.11; Lemma4.6 and proof of Theorem1.1, §4.3, pp.15–16

nodes.title: Marking lines under clutching and forgetting
nodes.statement: For every retained external label i, separating or nonseparating clutching pulls L_i on the target back canonically to the marking cotangent line on the vertex factor carrying i. These isomorphisms commute with marked-family isomorphisms, relabelling, iterated arbitrary base change, and permitted graph permutations. The marking-line conormal comparison L_i≅s_i*(I_i/I_i²) uses the smooth section; its dual is the section normal line. For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} the imported forgetful comparison π*L_i≅L_i(−D_{i,n+1}) is the morphism induced by contraction, with a simple zero along the rational-tail divisor. Its identity away from D and divisor description are compatible with the same pullback and relabelling conventions.
hypotheses: 2g−2+n>0 for the forgetful target; i is retained, and all source vertex types of a clutching map are stable.

D_{i,n+1} is the rational tail with marks i,n+1 and the attaching node, a Cartier divisor on the moduli stack. The comparison is pulled back as a line-bundle isomorphism even when a family maps into D.
The parent relative dualizing and Cartier-section inputs have locally Noetherian scope before the arbitrary-base extension R3; the final family interface requires that extension.
proofSteps: The parent gluing morphism is an isomorphism near every retained smooth section. Pull back relative differentials along that section and use the imported canonical identification s_i*ω≅s_i*Ω. This gives the retained-line comparison without choices of local coordinates.

Use the smooth-section conormal/differential comparison in R3; the ideal vanishes along the section, but its restriction I/I² is rank one. Parent base-change and gluing uniqueness give unit, composition, relabelling and graph-equivariance diagrams; descent uses the compatible-family formulation of stack QCoh.

For forgetting use the original MC.3/forget-cotangent-line endpoint with its source proof: Knudsen III Theorem4.1(c), pp.202–203, pulls the exact sequence to a section transverse to the exceptional divisor. The quotient has length one along D, so the map π*L_i→L_i has exactly that simple zero. This fixes the sign and hence L_i≅π*L_i⊗O(D). Do not reprove contraction or construct new ordinary sheaf tensor operations here.
acceptance: For M̄₀,₄→M̄₀,₃, π*L_i is trivial and D_{i,4} is one boundary section; thus L_i has degree1 on P¹, fixing the sign.
For retained marks on opposite sides of separating clutching, the two comparisons land on their respective factors. Self-clutching leaves every retained marking line unchanged.
Pullback along a constant map into D preserves the line-bundle identity; it does not preserve the effective-Cartier presentation as an embedding in that base.

For a proper family Sing is proper quasi-finite and hence finite. Keep its branch cover finite étale over a persistent-node base, not over an arbitrary smoothing base.

Import external/self gluing and their normalization/pushout universal properties. The reverse comparison needed here is relative partial normalization at ONE chosen persistent node, retaining all other nodes, finite and compatible with arbitrary base change, with a degree-two étale preimage and smooth branch sections after ordering. For split xy=0 the local algebra is R[x]×R[y] with equal constants recovering R[x,y]/xy. Require proper flat nodal cut families, étale-local constancy of the number of their connected components and of their genera/leg partition, and unit/counit/naturality on arrows. The current layer explicitly owns gluing and normalization properties; its field-normalization statement alone does not supply this full reverse contract.

Import the invertible nodal dualizing sheaf, its smooth-locus differential identification, smooth-section Cartier/conormal comparison, genus/cohomology base change and their canonical coherence. Extend the locally Noetherian construction to arbitrary family bases by finite-presentation approximation with descent independent of the Noetherian model. Ordinary scheme line tensor/dual/pullback operations must use the current AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0C and Jacobian ownership; MC.3 adds only moduli descent and comparisons.

remaining: R1–R3 are exact imports from the parent roadmap, with its arbitrary-base extension and relative cut/component statement still to be supplied. The present pass gives the moduli incidence, normalization and integral transition deductions conditional on those imports.

They remain explicit requested-stage endpoints; the moduli statements above are conditional on these contracts.

gaps.detail: The imported MC.0–MC.2 stable moduli and pointed chart targets still carry the original packet’s arbitrary-base cohomology, algebraization and representability obligations. SF.1 is not accepted at this checkout; stack-QCoh descent, quotient-stack and representability interfaces are imported as plans, never certified implementations. R09.5 normalization is an accepted plan but is also unimplemented. No stand-in Prop structure or geometric Lean axiom is used.

sourceIssues.printed: The stated separating closed-immersion assertion is made whenever the source genera differ or an external marking is present.
sourceIssues.correction: Keep finite unramified clutching, and distinguish the chosen node through the boundary normalization. A fixed separating type can have more than one preimage.
sourceIssues.reason: Three elliptic curves with distinct j-invariants in a chain, with one mark on the middle curve, give a genus-three one-pointed target. Cutting either outer node gives a preimage under M̄₁,₁×M̄₂,₂→M̄₃,₁. The first elliptic factors differ, so the two preimages are nonisomorphic. A closed immersion cannot have these two geometric preimages.
sourceIssues.known: Inherited confirmed finding StableReductionPartII/E3, REV-DESIGN-StableReductionPartII~2; no novelty claim in this follow-up.

upstreamNotes.detail: Current Layer1 explicitly displays DVR local node charts and field normalization. R1 asks for the arbitrary-base chart, and R2 spells out the reverse relative one-node cut needed by its Layer3 gluing/normalization promise. These are supplier refinements, not a second definition of nodal curves or scheme gluing.

Current L0A–L0C Suggested.lean already proposes tensor/pullback, duals and invertibleSheafEquivFiniteLocallyFreeRankOne; all ordinary scheme line operations stay there. No new sheaf tensor or determinant node is introduced. The atlas snapshot lacks this upstream roadmap, so its ownership is recorded here and inside R3 rather than fabricated as a library declaration.
